conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You came in with abdominal pain and high blood sugar. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi. Yeah, the pain in my upper belly is back—same as always. It’s from my gastroparesis or pancreatitis, I think. I’ve been vomiting at home, but not since I got here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Your blood sugar was very high—615—when you arrived. But your labs don’t show ketoacidosis. We gave you insulin and fluids in the ER. How have you been feeling since then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. The pain’s still there, but not as bad. I got some Dilaudid in the ER. That helped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep managing your pain with oral Dilaudid, as per your usual plan. No IV narcotics, since your primary doctor has set limits. We’ll also monitor your blood sugar closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s fine. I know the rules. But can I eat? I’m kind of hungry.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start you on clear liquids and see how you do. If you tolerate it, we can advance your diet. But avoid greasy or sugary foods—they can make your symptoms worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs from last night were mostly stable. Lipase was normal, which is reassuring—no sign of acute pancreatitis flare. Blood sugar this morning is 269.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s still high, right? My Lantus dose at home is 70 units, but I only took 40 last night because I wasn’t eating much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re giving you 50 units of Lantus at night while you’re here, plus a tighter sliding scale. We suspect you’re eating more regularly in the hospital, so we’ll adjust accordingly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. But I’ve been trying to stick to my routine. My port-a-cath is working fine for insulin, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your port is intact and we’re using it for meds. We’ll keep monitoring your sugars and adjust as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I noticed you had some pizza brought in. How did that sit with you?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I felt okay after. No vomiting. But my belly was a little more sore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’d recommend avoiding fried or fatty foods. They can worsen both gastroparesis and pancreatitis. Stick to lighter meals when possible.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll try. But it’s hard when visitors bring food.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a bladder scan, and it showed over 600 cc—quite full. You’re having trouble urinating?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve had this before. Urinary retention. It comes and goes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll need to straight catheterize you to empty your bladder. This could be from the narcotics, diphenhydramine, or just not moving around much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? I hate that. But okay, if I have to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your urine culture came back—just normal flora, no infection. We’ll keep monitoring your bladder. You may need a Foley if retention continues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I have to go home with a catheter?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not if we can help it. We’re hoping to get you voiding on your own. We’ll try removing the Foley later if things improve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Doctor, can I talk to someone? My roommate’s been hitting me. I’m scared to go back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m so sorry to hear that. I’ll get the social worker and domestic violence team to speak with you right away. You’re safe here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The social worker met with you. They’ll help you file a restraining order and find safer housing if needed. Is there anything else you’re worried about?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just getting my pain under control. And not going low on insulin. I had a bad low last week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re checking your sugars regularly. You’ve had a few lows, so we adjusted your sliding scale. We’re keeping your Lantus at 50 units for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood sugar has been more stable. We’re increasing your Lantus to 60 units tonight to better match your needs. How’s the pain today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still there, but I’m managing with the oral Dilaudid. I haven’t needed more than every 3 hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. And you’ve been eating without vomiting. That’s progress. We’ll keep working on getting your bladder function back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We removed the straight catheter. You were able to void about 400 cc. That’s a good sign. We’ll keep doing scans to make sure you’re emptying well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I don’t want to leave with a Foley.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll avoid it if possible. But if retention returns, we may need it temporarily. We also scheduled a urology follow-up for you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had two successful voids with post-void residuals under 100 cc. That’s excellent. We won’t need a Foley.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. That’s a relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your sugars are still fluctuating, but overall better. We’ll send you home on 60 units of Lantus at bedtime and your usual sliding scale.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my pain meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Same as before—Dilaudid 2 mg every 3 hours as needed. We’re giving you 20 tablets. No refills, per your contract.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand. I’ll stick to the plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today’s the day we’re planning to discharge you. You’re tolerating food, pain is stable, sugars are improving, and you’re urinating on your own.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. What about my anxiety? I’ve been using my Valium.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You can continue diazepam as needed—two 5 mg tablets every 8 hours. We’ve also adjusted some of your sleep meds to lower doses to reduce side effects.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my G-tube? It’s just for meds, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s in good condition. You’ll continue using it for medications as before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see your primary doctor this week. We’ve also set up an appointment with urology for your bladder issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge. Avoid fatty or sugary foods, take your meds as prescribed, and call your doctor if you have worsening pain, vomiting, or trouble urinating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And I’m going to file that restraining order. Thanks for listening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care of yourself. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One more thing—my sugars were high when I came in. Was that dangerous?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, 615 is very high, but you didn’t have ketoacidosis. Still, it’s important to manage it closely. That’s why we increased your Lantus dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll keep checking my sugars.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good plan. And remember, if you feel confused, dizzy, or shaky, check it right away—it could be low.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know. I’ve had lows before. I always carry juice.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. That’s exactly what to do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my asthma? I haven’t used my inhalers much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your lungs sounded clear. Keep using your fluticasone-salmeterol twice daily, and albuterol if you feel tight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Alright, the discharge papers are ready. A nurse will go over everything with you one more time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. I feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. Take care and stay safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll see you in follow-up. Call if anything changes before then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.
